newsitem.title: UK: Britons protest over Kurd camp closure plan.
newsitem.headline: Britons protest over Kurd camp closure plan.

text.p: British politicians and writers on Tuesday protested over United Nations plans to close a refugee camp in northern Iraq for 15,000 displaced Kurds.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR announced last month that it would phase out its operations at Atrush because of rebel activities in the camp.
Conservative politicians joined forces with lawmakers from the opposition Labour Party to issue a statement saying the closure "betrays a callous contempt for human rights."

Atrush was set up in 1994 for Kurds fleeing into northern Iraq from southeast Turkey, where villagers are caught in the middle of fighting between Turkish troops and the PKK (Kurdistan Workers Party guerrillas).

The statement, also signed by playwrights Tom Stoppard and Harold Pinter, said: "15,000 Kurdish refugees are now quietly and expeditiously sacrificed to suit Turkey's barbaric aims with the apparent approval of the UNHCR following Ankara's intervention in Washington.

"Atrush is no ordinary camp. It is the only sanctuary for approximately 15,000 Kurds from north Kurdistan (southeast Turkey) who fled the destruction of their villages and torture and brutal persecution carried out by Turkish gendarmes and soldiers in the last few years."
